glp1-action.title: How semaglutide works in the body
steps: Semaglutide travels in the blood, stuck to a protein called albumin. This keeps it working for days.
In the pancreas, it switches on beta cells. They release more insulin, mainly when blood sugar is high.
It also lowers glucagon, a hormone that raises blood sugar. This also happens mainly when sugar is high.
After a meal, food may leave the stomach a bit more slowly. This small effect seems to fade.
In animals, it reaches brain areas that control hunger. In people, trials show less hunger and smaller meals.
glp1-action.summary: Semaglutide lowers blood sugar when it is high and helps people eat less. These effects were measured in people. The stomach effect is small and seems to fade with time. Which brain areas take part comes mainly from animal studies.
glp1-action.caption: Semaglutide lowers blood sugar when it is high, and people feel less hungry.

insulin-glp1-hypo.title: Semaglutide with insulin or a sulfonylurea: the risk of low blood sugar
steps: Semaglutide alone lowers high blood sugar. Near normal, it works less, so sugar rarely gets too low.
Insulin lowers sugar too. So do tablets called sulfonylureas. They still work when sugar is normal or low.
Used together, they can push blood sugar too low. This is called hypoglycaemia.
So your prescriber may lower your dose of insulin or these tablets, as the label suggests.
Low sugar signs: sweating, shaking, hunger, confusion. Take sugar now. Can't swallow? Call an ambulance.
insulin-glp1-hypo.summary: On its own, semaglutide rarely makes blood sugar too low. With insulin or a sulfonylurea tablet it can, so the prescriber may lower those doses. Know the signs and take sugar at once. If the person cannot swallow, call an ambulance.
insulin-glp1-hypo.caption: On its own, semaglutide rarely makes sugar too low. With insulin or these tablets, it can.

glp1-class-hypo.title: GLP-1-type medicines (such as semaglutide or tirzepatide) with insulin or a sulfonylurea: the risk of low blood sugar
steps: Alone, a GLP-1-type medicine lowers high sugar. Near normal, it works less. Sugar rarely gets too low.
Insulin lowers sugar too. So do tablets called sulfonylureas. They still work when sugar is normal or low.
Used together, they can push blood sugar too low. This is called hypoglycaemia.
So the prescriber may lower the insulin or tablet dose. The labels suggest this.
Shaking, sweating or confused? Take sugar if the person can swallow. If not, call your local emergency number.
glp1-class-hypo.summary: On its own, a GLP-1-type medicine such as semaglutide or tirzepatide rarely makes blood sugar too low. With insulin or a sulfonylurea tablet it can, so the prescriber may lower the insulin or tablet dose. Know the signs and take sugar at once. If the person cannot swallow, call your local emergency number.

bpc-157-proposed-chain.title: The chain proposed for BPC-157, and where each step was seen
steps: Nobody knows where BPC-157 first acts on a cell. One 2026 study proposed a partner, not yet repeated.
In a dish, it raised signals in vessel cells, mostly in one lab. Human artery pieces relaxed too.
Tendon cells in a dish moved more and survived stress better. But they did not divide faster.
In injured rat tissue, more small blood vessels grew. Most of these studies come from one Zagreb group.
Rats healed faster in Zagreb studies. One tendon test by another lab found no clear strength gain.
In people, none of these steps has been shown. No controlled trial has been published in full.
bpc-157-proposed-chain.summary: The chain starts with a gap: no target for BPC-157 is established. In a dish it raised vessel signals and helped tendon cells move. In rats, more small vessels grew and tissue healed faster, mostly in one group's studies; one outside tendon test found no clear gain. None of this has been shown in people.
bpc-157-proposed-chain.caption: Some steps were seen in a dish or in rats. None has been shown in people.

angiogenesis-double-edge.title: New blood vessels help wounds heal, but tumours need them too
steps: In cells and rats, BPC-157 raised signals for new vessels. So did thymosin beta-4, which TB-500 comes from.
In injured rat tissue, new small blood vessels grew into the damaged area.
In many of those rat studies, the injured tissue healed faster.
Tumours need new blood vessels too. Without them, a tumour cannot grow beyond a tiny size.
Could these peptides feed a hidden tumour in people? This has never been tested.
angiogenesis-double-edge.summary: In cells and rats, BPC-157 and thymosin beta-4, the protein TB-500 comes from, helped new small blood vessels grow, and injured tissue often healed faster. Tumours also need new vessels to grow. Whether these peptides could help a hidden tumour grow in people has never been tested: it is a worry, not a finding.
angiogenesis-double-edge.caption: New vessels helped rat wounds heal. Tumours need new vessels too. In people, this risk is untested.

kpv-pept1-nfkb.title: How KPV is thought to calm inflammation, step by step
steps: KPV is a lab-made chain of three building blocks. They are the last three of the hormone alpha-MSH.
A doorway protein, PepT1, carries it into gut and immune cells. Inflamed gut has more PepT1.
Inside, it stops the switch NF-κB from reaching the cell's control centre, the nucleus.
So the cells make fewer of the signals that drive inflammation.
Mice with an inflamed gut recovered faster. In mice without PepT1, KPV no longer clearly reduced gut tumours.
In people, none of this has been tested. There is no human study of any kind.
kpv-pept1-nfkb.summary: In cells, KPV enters through the PepT1 doorway and keeps the inflammation switch NF-κB out of the nucleus, so the cells make fewer inflammation signals. Mice with an inflamed gut recovered faster, and the effect seems to need PepT1, at least in part. KPV has never been tested in people.
kpv-pept1-nfkb.caption: In cells and mice, KPV calms an inflammation switch. It has never been tested in people.

contamination-infection.title: How a needle can carry germs into the body
steps: Germs can sit on skin and on the rubber top of a vial. You cannot see them.
The needle goes through the skin. It can carry germs into the fat layer underneath.
Germs grow under the skin. They may form a pocket of pus (abscess), or redness spreads (cellulitis).
Germs can travel along a lymph vessel. Red lines on the skin can be a sign of this.
Germs in the blood can cause sepsis. Spreading redness, red lines, fever, feeling very ill? Get help now.
contamination-infection.summary: A needle can carry germs from the skin, the rubber top of a vial or the liquid into the fat under the skin. There they can form an abscess or cause cellulitis, spread along lymph vessels and reach the blood (sepsis). Spreading redness, red lines, fever or feeling very ill need a doctor straight away. With confusion, very fast breathing or blotchy skin, call your local emergency number.
contamination-infection.caption: A needle can carry germs under the skin. Spreading redness or fever? Get medical help quickly.

incretin-two-receptors.title: Tirzepatide: one medicine, two receptors
steps: Tirzepatide is one molecule that turns on two receptors: GLP-1 and GIP. Tests in cells show this.
GLP-1 receptor: more insulin and less glucagon when sugar is high. Less hunger. The stomach slows at first.
The GIP receptor also raises insulin when sugar is high. Fat and brain effects were seen in animals.
In two trials, people lost more weight on tirzepatide than semaglutide. In diabetes, blood sugar fell more too.
How much the GIP part adds is not known. We found no study in people that tests it.
incretin-two-receptors.summary: Tirzepatide turns on the GLP-1 and the GIP receptor. Through GLP-1 it raises insulin when sugar is high, lowers glucagon and hunger, and slows the stomach at first. Which brain areas take part comes mainly from animal studies. GIP also raises insulin; its effects on fat and the brain come from mice. In two open-label trials against semaglutide, weight fell more with tirzepatide (1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes; 751 adults with obesity), and HbA1c fell more in the diabetes trial. How much the GIP part adds is not known.
incretin-two-receptors.caption: Tirzepatide acts on two receptors. In trials, weight and blood sugar fell more than with semaglutide.

incretin-three-receptors.title: Retatrutide: one molecule, three receptors
steps: Retatrutide is one molecule that turns on three receptors: GLP-1, GIP and glucagon. Cell tests show this.
Its GLP-1 and GIP parts raise insulin when sugar is high. In trials, people felt less hungry.
The glucagon receptor acts mainly on the liver. In a trial liver fat fell, partly through weight loss.
In mice, the glucagon part made the body burn more energy. No results in people are published yet.
Trials showed large weight loss. Glucagon's share in this is not known. It is not an approved medicine.
incretin-three-receptors.summary: Retatrutide turns on the GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors. In trials, people felt less hungry, blood sugar and liver fat fell, and weight fell a lot (TRIUMPH-1: 2,339 adults with obesity, 80 weeks). Which brain areas take part comes mainly from animal studies. Extra energy use was shown in mice; no results in people are published yet. How much the glucagon part adds is not known. As of 20 October 2026, no country has approved it as a medicine.
incretin-three-receptors.caption: Retatrutide acts on three receptors. Trials show large weight loss. It is not an approved medicine.
